Medibytes — Technical Design Document
Draft 0.1 · 2 September 2026 · Derived from Medibytes PRD v1.0 (29 August 2026)
Design for the MVP: voice dictation → structured discharge summary → the hospital's own
form, for admitted patients.
This is a standalone document. It contains no cross-links and depends on no other file.
Section references use §numbers. Requirement identifiers ( FR-* , NFR-* ) refer to the
Medibytes PRD v1.0 and are reproduced in the traceability matrix at Appendix A.
0. About this document
0.1 What this is, and what it is not
This is a first draft, circulated for team review. It is not yet a handoff document, and it should
not be given to an implementing engineer as though it were finished.
The reason is specific and is stated plainly rather than buried: five one-way architectural
decisions are still open (Appendix C). They are written up with options and trade-offs, but
none has been ruled on. Where this design depends on one, it does one of two things:
It does not pick, and it does not quietly assume. Deciding those five is the work between this
draft and a handoff-ready document.

0.5 A defect in the source document, carried here
PRD §0.2 states that every requirement carries a MoSCoW priority and acceptance criteria.
The five NFR tables carry neither. All 37 non-functional requirements are stated as targets
with no priority and no acceptance test.
For four of them the PRD's §9.1 definition of done supplies a gate. For the remaining 33 —
including all twelve NFR-SEC-* — there is no stated bar for "done". This design proposes a
mechanism and a measurement point for each (§10, §11), but a measurement point is not an
acceptance criterion, and someone must decide the threshold at which each is considered
met. Recorded as gap G-19.

1.4 The one property that outranks everything
PRD §7.4: zero record cross-contamination — a document attached to the wrong patient or
admission — is a hard stop, not a target. One incident halts rollout.
A ward holds many patients open simultaneously, which makes this more dangerous than in an
outpatient setting, not less. This design treats patient/admission binding as a correctness
problem with its own invariants (§4.3), its own failure-mode rows (§9) and its own tests (§13.2)
— never as a user-interface concern.

2.2 Design non-goals
Things a competent engineer might reasonably build, and should not.
2.3 Constraints
A generic clinical data platform. One document type, one workflow. The extension points
in §7.6 are the whole of the generality being bought.
An offline-first application. PRD NFR-REL-05 requires that intermittent connectivity not
block capture, with a 4-hour buffer. It does not require offline patient registration, offline
review or offline sign-off, and those must not be built — offline sync is the highest-risk
correctness area in the system and its surface is deliberately kept to one queue (§6.2).
A real-time collaborative editor. One clinician edits one draft. Concurrent editing is
handled by detection and refusal (§9), not by merge.
An HMIS integration. Tier 0 is printed output matching the hospital's form, and it must work
with zero cooperation from the incumbent vendor. No API is assumed to exist.
A microservice architecture. Two services exist because the Python ML ecosystem has
no Node equivalent, not as a scaling strategy. The boundary is strict: Python owns audio
and model calls and nothing else. Business logic drifting into the AI service is a design
defect.
Analytics infrastructure. FR-ADM-03 's dashboard reads from the operational store. At
MVP volume nothing else is warranted.

4.8 Migrations
Forward-only, versioned, applied at deploy before the new container serves traffic. Every
migration is reversible in principle but rollback is by restore, not by down-migration — at three
hospitals with one engineer, a tested restore (§12.4) is more reliable than a down-migration

Mutating endpoints accept Idempotency-Key . The key, request hash and response are

15. Design objections
Stated in writing rather than absorbed silently, per the principle that silent compliance is how
projects fail six months in.
15.1 The critical path is one person, and it is the whole design
Units 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 are sequential, all led by the tech lead, and together they are
the product. The interns' work (units 4, 13, 14, 16) is genuinely parallel but does not shorten the
path.
Consequence: the schedule has no slack against a single absence, and risk R-7 (key-person)
is not merely a personnel risk — it is a schedule dependency with no mitigation in the current
plan beyond documentation discipline.

Options: bring the first junior engineer forward from month 8 if runway permits; or accept the
risk explicitly and in writing, with the founders retaining enough technical context to survive a
departure.
15.2 Three of the four gating benchmarks are uncollected, and one
gates the build itself
NFR-PER-06/07/08 are unbenchmarked because V4 and V5 have not been collected. The
PRD is unambiguous: if NFR-PER-06 cannot be met on real audio, stop and re-scope.
This design cannot resolve that, and it should not be read as evidence the risk has been
retired. Units 6 and 10 assume a provider that meets the target exists. If none does, §7
changes shape entirely and the 14-week Phase 1 estimate is void.
Recommendation: unit 6 (benchmark harness) runs before unit 10 and ideally before unit 8,
so the answer arrives while the design can still absorb it.
15.3 The infrastructure budget and the capacity figures may not be
consistent
[E] ~₹18,000/month covers a single VM running the application, AI service, datastore, Redis
and object storage. That is plausible at NFR-REL-04 's stated 200 documents/day. It is less
obviously plausible at the ~360/day the cost model assumes (gap G-05), and it makes no
allowance for the AI service scaling horizontally as NFR-REL-06 requires.
This is a real conflict between two [E] figures, not a rounding difference. It should be
settled before unit 19, and it is a commercial question — cost per document is a stated margin
metric — as much as a technical one.
15.4 Deferred consent is a design constraint that grows
FR-PAT-06 is deferred. The exposure is small while dictation is a clinician speaking alone at a
workstation and grows the moment capture moves to the bedside, where a patient may be
audible.
FR-ADM-08 ships as the configuration hook, which is correct. But this design does not treat
consent as a first-class entity, and retrofitting it after a hospital is live means backfilling consent
state for existing admissions. Flagged so the decision is deliberate.
15.5 One document type, seven promised
Rule 3 is sound discipline. But NFR-MNT-05 's obligation — schema, mapping, acceptance
criteria and labelled test set per type, versioned together — means every new document type

carries a permanent testing cost, not a one-off build cost. At seven types that is a standing
obligation the current team size does not obviously absorb.
ADR-005 addresses the build cost. It does not address the maintenance cost, and nothing in
the project's planning notes budgets for it.
